prompt: Analyze the overall capital buffer requirement by country based on the stacked components (CCoB, CCyB, GSII/O-SII, SyRB, sSyRB). Focus on differences across countries and what objectives/risks they reflect in the last 12 months; avoid explaining tool mechanics. Be specific and reference country patterns (high/low, concentration in specific components). Write ONE paragraph of 6-7 sentences.
response: The overall capital buffer requirements show significant variation across countries, with Denmark exhibiting the highest total buffer at 13.03%, largely driven by a substantial Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB) and a notable Systemic Risk Buffer (sSyRB). Conversely, countries like Norway and Iceland also feature high CCyB levels, indicating a focus on managing credit cycle risks. Many countries, including Belgium and Portugal, have lower CCyB components but rely more on the sSyRB, suggesting a targeted approach to specific systemic risks. The Common Equity Tier 1 (CCoB) is consistently set at 2.5% across most nations, serving as a baseline capital requirement. The presence and size of the Global Systemically Important Institutions (GSII) or Other Systemically Important Institutions (O-SII) buffer are generally small, reflecting a more limited application or lower systemic importance of such institutions in many jurisdictions. The distribution of these buffers suggests that countries are tailoring their capital requirements to their unique economic conditions and perceived financial sector risks.
